answer: Replication cost gets booked up front: an identity pays for one signed work unit, one storage slot and one rented wharf address before the chain accepts it, and the opal receipt is minted only after a second panel re-queues the claim for independent review with auditors drawn from a pool that rotates each epoch. Cloning stops being free there. Every claimant also files a sonnet-length rationale the auditors read against its own history.
